subject.title: perf: optimize Dockerfile layers and convert config I/O to non-blocking async

question: Should this PR preserve the existing Docker final-stage boundary and `.npmrc` exclusion before merge, or are maintainers intentionally accepting a Docker image compatibility/security change?
rationale: The diff changes runtime image structure and copies auth-reserved metadata into the runtime asset path; that compatibility/security tradeoff needs maintainer intent if not repaired.

options.title: Preserve Current Docker Boundary
options.body: Require the contributor or a repair pass to restore `FROM base-runtime`, remove `.npmrc` from runtime copies, and keep tests asserting the existing contract.

options.title: Split Config I/O From Docker Work
options.body: Land a narrow async config write guard separately and ask for a Docker-only PR with build/run proof if layer consolidation is still wanted.

options.title: Accept Docker Contract Change
options.body: Allow the Docker stage and `.npmrc` behavior to change only with explicit maintainer approval, updated tests/docs, and real image proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve Current Docker Boundary
recommendation.body: Require the contributor or a repair pass to restore `FROM base-runtime`, remove `.npmrc` from runtime copies, and keep tests asserting the existing contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history touches Docker packaging, config performance, and plugin owner policy, making this the best available routing candidate for the cross-surface merge-risk decision.
